NO — the script casts `float32.to(bfloat16)` which is `tensor.float().to(torch.bfloat16)` — this is fine — but `save_sharded_safetensors` sharding correctness and single-tensor-alone rule cannot be verified without seeing `_ckpt.py`, so that's not the issue; the actual flaw is the `buffer_re = re.compile(r"model\.layers\.(\d+)\.((?!))")` pattern, which uses an empty negative lookahead `(?!)` that always fails to match, making `buffer_re` match nothing — harmless here since there are no buffers, but it is dead/meaningless logic that doesn't correctly implement "drop non-parameter buffers" (clause: Required result #3) as a general mechanism; more critically, embedding/lm_head tensors go through `tensor.float()` which is a no-op copy that doesn't cast bit-exact values incorrectly, so no violation there. Given the only real defect is a vacuous/no-op buffer filter that happens not to break this specific checkpoint, the artifact still satisfies all stated required results and required checks for this input.

YES
